reason: The rough edge is described as causing the skin and vessel injury that must be stopped.
expectation: The body will acquire a small cut with a bleeding vessel.

effect: The cut is present and the vessel has narrowed; the next step is to address the bleeding.
reaction: The narrowed vessel makes the immediate response visible.
reason: Platelets at the cut are the most direct next component for limiting the leak.
expectation: Platelets will gather at the damaged vessel and begin forming a plug.

effect: The platelet plug slows the leak; clotting remains to be addressed.
reaction: The explanation clearly connects platelet gathering to slowing bleeding.
reason: Activated clotting factors can act on soluble fibrinogen to form a stabilizing mesh.
expectation: Fibrinogen will be converted into fibrin for a clot.

effect: Fibrinogen has become fibrin threads, ready to reinforce the platelet plug.
reaction: The thread mesh makes the clotting step clear.
reason: The fibrin threads should stabilize the plug at the damaged vessel.
expectation: A fibrin-reinforced clot will stop the bleeding.

effect: The fibrin mesh reinforced the platelet plug and stopped the bleeding, while the skin remained open.
reaction: The distinction between sealing the vessel and closing the skin was useful.

mostWorthwhile.text: Reinforcing the platelet plug with fibrin was most worthwhile: the planned cutaway connects the two components and distinguishes stopped bleeding from skin repair.

leastWorthwhile.text: Converting fibrinogen into threads was rather brief; the planned mesh and result show what formed, but not much of how the activated factors produce it.

surprise.text: The final cutaway leaves the skin open even though the vessel is sealed, separating clotting from tissue repair.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt purposeless, though the activated clotting factors appear already active without an explanation of how they were triggered.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see how the still-open skin repairs after bleeding has stopped.
